category_title: Low-achieving students with disruptive behaviors and high absenteeism
minimal_context: The student is asked to read a fictional story about a cauldron and formulate questions in their notebook while sitting in a U-shaped arrangement.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Please read the story about the cauldron and write down some questions in your notebooks.

STUDENT: Welcome to the hell. (Turns around and starts talking loudly to a friend instead of looking at the stimulus materials)

TUTOR: You need to stay quiet and listen to the instructions.

STUDENT: (Stands up from the U-shaped seating arrangement) I don't want to just stay quiet and listen to you.

TUTOR: Please sit back down at your place and stop disturbing your friends.

STUDENT: (Starts walking toward the classroom door) I'm not doing this. I can get out of class anytime I feel like it.

options.A: Explicitly teach reading comprehension strategies and the thinking that facilitates text-to-self, text-to-text, and text-to-world connections when reading the stimulus materials.
options.B: Integrate film into the philosophical inquiry sessions to support literacy learning and avoid teaching the stimulus materials from a purely factual perspective.
options.C: Adjust the ratio of lower-level to higher-level questions based on the student's reading level during the philosophical inquiry sessions.
options.D: Praise the student for good behavior, specifically when they focus and show interest in completing the question-formulation tasks.
